net.lemnik.eodsql

Enum GeneratedKeys

  • java.lang.Object
    • java.lang.Enum<GeneratedKeys>
      • net.lemnik.eodsql.GeneratedKeys
  • All Implemented Interfaces:
    Serializable, Comparable<GeneratedKeys>

    public enum GeneratedKeys
extends Enum<GeneratedKeys>
    Enumeration used by the @Update annotation to specify what to do with keys generated by the database.
    Author:
    Jason Morris
    See Also:
    Update, AutoGeneratedKeys

    • Enum Constant Detail

      • NO_KEYS_RETURNED

        public static final GeneratedKeys NO_KEYS_RETURNED

        Specifies that a normal Statement.executeUpdate(java.lang.String) should be performed. In this case no keys will be requested from the database, and any that are returned will be ignored.

        This is the default value, and is mostly used with the SQL statement is an "UPDATE" or when you are generating the primary key in your application instead of in the database.

      • RETURNED_KEYS_DRIVER_DEFINED

        public static final GeneratedKeys RETURNED_KEYS_DRIVER_DEFINED

        Specifies that the JDBC driver should return whatever keys it decides to. This is the equivalent of Statement.executeUpdate(String sql, Statement.RETURN_GENERATED_KEYS)

        Databases that have the ability to auto-generate keys will generally respond to this call with the columns they have constructed as part of the "INSERT" query. Columns returned from the database will be bound to the fields in the returned objects by their column names (the same way as is done with non-key objects). Thus the names of the columns returned by the database is significant.

        Many JDBC drivers will return only simple primary keys, and will not name the column as expected (if it is named at all). In this case the RETURNED_KEYS_FIRST_COLUMN value should be used, as it works in a similar way, but ignores the column names returned.

        See Also:
        Statement.execute(String, int), RETURNED_KEYS_FIRST_COLUMN

      • RETURNED_KEYS_COLUMNS_SPECIFIED

        public static final GeneratedKeys RETURNED_KEYS_COLUMNS_SPECIFIED

        This specifies that the generated keys should be explicitly requested from the JDBC driver by name. This is the equivalent of Statement.executeUpdate(String sql, String [] colNames)

        Many JDBC drivers don't have this functionality and will throw an Exception if this value is used for an update.

        See Also:
        Statement.execute(String, String[])

      • RETURNED_KEYS_FIRST_COLUMN

        public static final GeneratedKeys RETURNED_KEYS_FIRST_COLUMN

        Specifies that the the first column from of the generated keys should be mapped as the AutoGeneratedKeys. Several JDBC drivers don't handle the returning of more than one generated key, and often don't support returning the key with it's real column name. This flag can be used to work around such drivers.

        This option can also be used as an optimization when a non-composite auto-generated key is being used (which is most of the time).

        Since:
        1.1
        See Also:
        Statement.execute(String, int)
